checklist.note: The decision list's terminal branch is the most privileged outcome (human_typed), and the only thing standing between an agent-run authorization and that outcome is a substring test over text the agent writes. Rules 1 and 2 are fail-closed; rule 4 is fail-open, and it is the one every non-matching case lands in. Also: single-file breadcrumb cannot survive concurrent Bash tool calls; multi-adapter hook-installed resolution is unspecified; and ownership of the consume-on-match delete is stated two ways.
Matching the parsed --reason value as a verbatim substring of the raw shell command line is not a sound predicate — quoting, escaping and expansion break it in the permissive direction.

The tier-1 single-reader check forbids the path literal outside core/authorization_channel.py, but the breadcrumb hook entry needs an identifying marker whose only available substring is that path, and _settings_merge.py's established convention is module-level marker constants. No home is stated.

Acceptance obligations track the body: the four outcomes, both precedence orderings, the window's lower bound, consume/expiry, malformed input, attest verify on real events, and the live disclosure this cut expects to trigger. The gate removal, breadcrumb, seam, rollup, blocker, hint rewrite and doc set all appear in Scope.

findings.summary: Rule 4 makes `human_typed` the fallthrough, so any agent-run authorization the text predicate fails to match is silently recorded as a human act with no disclosure. The doc closes uninstall-laundering (rule 1) and pty-forgery (rule 2) but not indirection: the agent writes the breadcrumb unavoidably, yet fully controls its *content*. `bash -c 'super-harness review authorize ...'` inside a wrapper script, `sleep 6 && super-harness review authorize ...` (mtime falls outside the window), or building the command from a shell variable all leave a breadcrumb whose text lacks `review authorize` and/or the reason — no match, no TTY, therefore `human_typed`, therefore no merge blocker. The design's own teeth (a count a human can falsify from memory) read zero. The terminal branch of a security decision list must be the fail-closed one; `human_typed` should be reachable only on positive evidence, with `unknown` as the default.

One overwritten file cannot carry per-invocation evidence when tool calls run concurrently. Claude Code issues multiple Bash calls in a single assistant message (this repo's own agent instructions encourage it). If the agent issues `review authorize` alongside any sibling Bash call, the sibling's PreToolUse hook overwrites the breadcrumb with unrelated command text, and its mtime may also land after `process_start` — violating the window's upper bound. Either way the match fails and the agent-run authorization resolves `human_typed` with no adversarial intent required. The design never states what happens when N breadcrumbs compete for one path; a per-invocation-keyed file, or an append-with-scan, is needed for the predicate to mean what §3 claims.

`breadcrumb_hook_installed` is resolved "over the adapters recorded in adapters.yaml" but the combination rule across multiple agent adapters is never stated, and `adapters/registry.py` explicitly supports a flat list holding both `claude-code` and `codex`. Any-True and All-True give opposite answers with opposite safety properties: with any-True, a repo registering both adapters treats the hook as installed, so a Codex-run authorization (no breadcrumb hook on that host, no TTY) resolves `human_typed` and never discloses — exactly the laundering rule 1 exists to prevent, reachable by registering a second adapter. With All-True, the same repo resolves `unknown` for every authorization including genuine human ones. Two implementers will read this line differently and one of the readings is silently permissive.

The match requires this invocation's `--reason` string to appear verbatim in the breadcrumb's command text, but the breadcrumb holds the raw pre-shell command line while `--reason` is the post-shell parsed value; the two are not equal in general. A reason containing an embedded double quote (`--reason "he said \"no\""`), a `$`-sequence, a backslash, a line continuation, or a value assembled from a variable or heredoc yields a parsed string that is not a substring of the raw text. The predicate then fails on a genuine agent invocation and rule 4 records `human_typed` — a silent, accidental escalation to the undisclosed channel, triggered by ordinary punctuation in a human-written sentence.

Consume-on-match has two stated owners and one stated prohibition. §3 says "the resolver additionally deletes the breadcrumb on match"; Scope line 317 says `core/authorization_channel.py` is Pure and only "returns the channel plus the evidence dict"; Scope line 328 says `cli/review.py` "consumes a matched breadcrumb". An implementer following the module contract will leave the delete to the CLI, one following §3 will put it in the resolver, and one reading both may leave it to the other and ship neither. If neither deletes, the bound §3 relies on ("a single stale entry can mislead at most one invocation") is gone: one stale breadcrumb misclassifies every authorization with the same reason inside the window. The order also matters and is unstated — deleting before the event is appended loses the evidence on a crash.

The breadcrumb PreToolUse entry needs a path-independent marker so `_strip_entries` / `restore_or_remove_managed_hooks` can identify it, but the hook command is only `cat > <abs>/.harness/.last-agent-bash.json`, so the sole identifying substring is the path literal — which the tier-1 check at the end of this document forbids in any `src/super_harness` file other than `core/authorization_channel.py`. `_settings_merge.py`'s established convention (`_OURS_MARKER`, `_SESSION_OURS_MARKER`, `_STOP_OURS_MARKER`) is exactly a module-level literal. The design carves out only `claude_code.py` importing the constant, and says nothing about the marker, so an implementer following local convention writes code the change's own ratified decision rejects at merge and has to rework it (thread the marker in as a required kwarg, or add a distinct comment marker to the command).

Hostile-input handling on the rendered row is otherwise thorough — AUTH-004/005/008 vectors (newline, tab, C0/C1 escapes, bidi override) are all closed by the `str.isprintable()` whitelist, per-field rather than per-row, with non-ASCII text preserved and `--json` carrying the recorded bytes (`asdict` recurses into the tuple of records). AUTH-010 is the residue: two fields interpolated into the row are not type-guarded the way `reviewer`/`reason` are.

`docs/cli-reference.md` is regenerated from the generator, AGENTS.md matches the adapter string exactly, and the §Scope list now names `cli/status.py` and the three additional test files. `docs/getting-started.md`, `docs/concepts.md` and `docs/state-machine.md` were re-checked: their only `review authorize` mention carries no TTY claim, and their TTY sentences are about `review human confirm`'s nonce and `init`'s wizard, both deliberately unchanged.

findings.summary: `_authorization_row` passes `a.actor` and `a.change_id` to `_one_line` unguarded, while `derive_authorizations` type-guards only `reviewer` and `reason` (`isinstance(x, str)`). `parse_event_line` does not enforce str for either of the unguarded fields: `actor.identifier` is validated only with `"identifier" not in actor_raw`, and `change_id` only with a truthiness check — so `{"actor": {"type": "human", "identifier": null}}` or `"change_id": 7` parses fine and yields `AuthorizationRecord(actor=None)` / `change_id=7`, despite both being annotated `str`. `_one_line` then evaluates `"".join(c ... for c in None)` and raises `TypeError`, which is uncaught: `report_cmd` invokes `_render_human` directly, so the whole command tracebacks and every other band of the report is lost with it. That contradicts the two rules this code states for itself — `value_report.py`'s module law that the report never crashes, and `derive_authorizations`' "Never raises … silently losing an authorization is the one failure mode that cannot be tolerated here" — since an unrenderable report loses all of them. The timestamp field is safe (`parse_event_line` does enforce str there, and `parse_ts` normalises offsets to real UTC, so the `UTC` label is honest). Reachability is a hand-edited or foreign-written `events.jsonl` rather than anything the harness emits, which is why this is minor and not major; the fix is the same one-line `isinstance` shape already applied to `reviewer`, or coercing with `str()` inside `_one_line`.

`cli/errors.py`'s module docstring is an explicit style contract for hints — "Start with an imperative verb", "Sentence-cased: first letter uppercase, trailing period", "One sentence; if longer guidance is needed, prefer a `Docs:` link via `docs_anchor=` instead of running multi-line in the hint" — and closes with "Examples (all current call sites follow this shape)". The new hint breaks three of those clauses at once (lowercase `relay`, no trailing period, an embedded `\n` plus an 8-space continuation) and a repo-wide search confirms it is the only multi-line hint that exists, so the parenthetical claim about all call sites is now false. The rendered text is fine and is exactly what the design specified; the defect is that the deviation was not reconciled with the guide, leaving the next author to read a rule the codebase no longer keeps and either propagate a contradiction or "fix" this hint back into a shape the design rejected. Either carve the command-to-be-typed case into the guide (one line: a hint whose payload is a copy-pasteable command may run to a second indented line) or note the exception at the call site.

prior_findings.note: Closed, and closed as a whitelist rather than a third blacklist — which is the right direction given that the two prior rounds each excluded one more class and each missed the next. `_one_line` now maps every character where `str.isprintable()` is False to a space before the whitespace collapse, which covers the named `\x1b[1A\x1b[2K` cursor-move vector, the C0/C1 range generally, the bidi overrides, NBSP, and the earlier rounds' newlines and tabs in one rule. Verified against the tests: `test_report_human_row_survives_control_characters` asserts no `\x1b` survives and that the text is neutralised rather than dropped (`quiet [1A [2Kgone`), `test_report_human_row_survives_a_bidi_override` covers RLO, `test_report_human_row_keeps_non_ascii_text_intact` proves the whitelist is not a latin-1 filter (Chinese plus an emoji round-trip), and `test_report_json_keeps_control_characters_as_recorded` pins that the neutralisation stays a rendering rule — `--json` still carries the recorded bytes, exactly as the AUTH-004 note argued. Applied per field, so the hostile value cannot be `actor` or an unparseable timestamp either.

`## Scope` now lists `cli/status.py` with the reason, and it does more than patch the omission: it states that the exhausted-budget `next_command` carried the same "in a human-owned TTY" clause, that no test held it, and that it was found by code review rather than by the document — naming the specific gap that the "checked rather than assumed" paragraph swept `docs/*.md` and never swept the `.py` surfaces printing the same sentence. The three missing test files are also listed (`test_review_runs.py`, `test_value_report.py`, `test_claude_code.py`, plus `tests/integration/cli/test_status.py`), so the list is exhaustive again against the actual diff. The requested §3 sentence is present too: "That sentence is printed at two decision points, not one", followed by the `status` `next_command` explanation — so §3 no longer describes one surface while the file list denies the second.
